answer: A stake-bonded reputation works like a pearl forming inside an oyster: an agent must lock real value before it can trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs a fortune. Honest agents grow a vine of verifiable attestations - each completed task adds a link others can check - while a fake identity has no history and earns no trust. An attacker facing this dune of rising costs finds every new identity starts at zero reputation and must pay the same bond again, making Sybil attacks unprofitable while legitimate agents compound their standing.
